items.title: [Bug]: LoRA on MLA kv_b_proj is silently never applied — decode bypasses it via absorption, prefill via a stale pre-wrap reference
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.25.1 (V1), reproduced conceptually on current `main` (file refs below are `main`). Applies to any MLA model (DeepSeek V2/V3/R1/V3.2, GLM MoE DSA, Kimi K2) with an adapter targeting `kv_b_proj`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

An adapter containing `kv_b_proj` LoRA tensors loads without error and is applied **nowhere**. The LoRA manager wraps the layer, but the wrapper's `forward()` is never invoked on any path:

- **Decode (absorbed/MQA):** attention consumes `W_UK`/`W_UV`, split from the raw `kv_b_proj` weight at load time, via BMMs (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:822`, `:1075`). No LoRA indirection exists in this path.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache: backend advertises a kernel block size the kernels do not use
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

### Evidence (8x MI350X, gfx950, TP8, ROCm 7.2.3, `index_kpool=4`, `block_size=640`)

Instrumented at the indexer, two identical requests, prefix caching off:

| | before | after fix |
|---|---|---|
| distinct cache slots written (of 4096 pools) | **864** | **4096** |
| `max_slot` | 863 (= 26x32+31) | 4159 (= 26x

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**.

The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's.

Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below.

### Measurements

GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash indexer block-table mismatch on gfx942
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Environment

- 8x MI308X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev628+g2a02f6efe.rocm723`, `amd_aiter==0.1.21.post2`, `flydsl==0.3.2`
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8, bf16 KV, prefix caching enabled
- `index_kpool=4`, `index_topk=2048`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`

## 1. Indexer block-table granularity mismatch

Long-prompt requests completed, but recall near the end degraded. The indexer cache uses 128-token storage pages (32 pooled entries), while the block table uses 640-token manager blocks:

- `allocate_kv_cache` honors `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size`.
- `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` does not, leaving manager block IDs where physical page IDs are needed.

At `max_model_len=262144`, the 410-column table can address only `410 * 32 * 4 = 52480` token positions when interpreted by the pool-page consumer. This is a layout mismatch, not a model context-length limit.

Observed before the fix:

```text
cache_shape=(91780, 32, 132)  block_table_shape=(1, 410)
required_pooled_entries=40160
last_query_position=160639  max_selected_token_index=52479
```

Outside the table width, the gather masks the block-ID read and writes a zero scale. Inside the width, manager block IDs can name the wrong physical pages; this is not a fixed token offset.

PR #56381 makes the table use storage-page granularity. At the **same 262144-token setting**, it becomes `(1, 2050)`; manager block `b` expands to pages `5*b + [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`.

## 2. Separate kpool-tail slot-mapping fault

A 7680-token prefill step also produced GPU memory-access faults. With `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`, the stack pointed to `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`.

`KpoolTailSpec` reserves one circular block per request, but the generic mapper uses `position // 4` against a 32-column row. Its mapping should be left to `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder`. Fault occurrence depends on allocation; 7680 is an observed step size, not a universal threshold.

**PR #56381 addresses only problem 1.**

items.bodyExcerpt:
### TL;DR

On GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool sparse indexer, ROCm aiter path), per-layer top-k selection frequently drops the most recent context pools at long prompt lengths — even with a correct block table. The config sets `always_select_tail=True`, but the only tail the selection machinery guarantees is the ≤3-token *incomplete* pool; complete recent pools compete in the top-k like everything else and can rank below the `index_topk=2048` cutoff. Tail-of-context retrieval then fails non-deterministically. Forcing the last 128 pools (512 tokens, 25% of the budget) into every layer's selection fixed all our failing lengths up to the full 256K context.

### Setup

GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16, vLLM `0.31.0.dev0+git73859fec` (Sep-28 pin), TP=2 (ray across 2× AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Strix Halo, gfx1151), aiter sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4, `max_model_len` 262144. Probe: needle ("Paris") in the final line, a single neutral decoy ("Berlin") in the first line, forced tool-call response, lengths 12K–255K prompt tokens.

- With the block-table granularity bug (#58858, fix in #59412) corrected on our tree (gather-site table expansion), tail retrieval still failed non-deterministically: ~12K ≈50/50, 54K ≈50/50, 75K FAIL, 105K FAIL (multiple runs each).
- Instrumenting the selection (per-layer, last query row of the failing chunk): the last token is always selected (the forced incomplete pool), but coverage of the last 48 positions varies per layer — e.g. **2, 6, 22, 30, 34, 42 of 48** across the 11–12 sparse layers. items.title: [Bug]: HiSparse: long prefill batched with decodes can OOM a running server
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec (re-confirmed on 12b005eefa), 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse, a long prompt batched with running decodes can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and the running requests die with it. This happens even when all of the prompt's KV is on GPU.

In a mixed decode/prefill batch, the prefill rows don't read the GPU-resident pages directly. Instead:
- the prefilling request's entire history is copied into a temporary GPU buffer on every layer (`stage_prefill_rows`), about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens;
- decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens.

Neither allocation is needed when every page is GPU-resident, and startup profiling reserves neither. The cause is the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition: it was in the FlashInfer, FlashAttn and SM120 backends, and since #55866 it lives in the shared `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mqa`. FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill.

**Not a risk: prompts that spill to host** (e.g. a 1M-token prefill misrouted to a HiSparse decoder). The history copy is required there and unreserved, but it is capped by `max_model_len` (one layer at a time). On GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 with the prompt forced to spill (util 0.90, 24 decodes), main completes with the per-step peak only 0.88 GiB over the profiled peak, well within headroom. #60424 tried to reserve it and was closed.

items.title: [RFC]: A standard for MonoKernels in vllm/models
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

A **MonoKernel** is a persistent kernel that runs most or all of one decoder layer's decode step in a single launch. This RFC proposes one way to add them under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`:

- The layer loop calls `mono.forward_layer(...)`, which launches the layer's kernel or calls the vLLM layer unchanged. The module tree and parameter names never change.
- A shared library, `vllm/models/common/mono/` (~650 lines), owns what every MonoKernel repeats: refusals, routing, fail-stop, health words, peer memory, cache re-binding.
- A model adds its kernel plus ~400 lines, instead of a 6–24k-line stack of its own.

The standard starts ROCm-only, where all known MonoKernels live (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3). CUDA joins with a CUDA co-author.

#### Why MonoKernels

At low concurrency, decode is bound by launch overhead and weight reads, and a MonoKernel removes most of both. On 8× MI350X a graph-mode GLM-5.2 decode step issues ~2,459 kernels in vLLM. With the MonoKernel it issues ~210: 75 MonoKernel launches plus ~135 for dense layers 0–2, input prep and the head.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

**TL;DR:** Resize video frames right after decoding instead of in the HF processor. For Qwen3-VL on 1080p video: 10–60× smaller frame arrays, 35–46% less decode + processor time, 1.8–2.5× throughput when preprocessing-bound, and `pixel_values_videos` stays bit-identical.

**Problem.** vLLM's video loaders keep every sampled frame at full resolution; the HF processor then copies and resizes them. Most video processors downscale (Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, GLM-4.xV, LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL, ...). For Qwen3-VL, a 5-min 1080p video at 2 fps is 600 frames ≈ 3.5 GiB per request, resized down to 256×128 (W×H).

**Proposal.** Resize each frame right after decoding, using the same op and target size as the HF processor (Qwen3-VL: torchvision bicubic + antialias on uint8, size from `smart_resize`). The processor then computes the same target size from the already-resized frames, so its resize changes nothing and `pixel_values_videos` is bit-identical. That holds for common aspect ratios but not always (e.g. 480×1920 with ≥258 frames shrinks one more step), so the loader checks it and otherwise keeps the current path. The resize is generic; each model only supplies its target size. Starting with Qwen3-VL, the only one measured so far.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Fix streaming tool-call args truncated by schema coercion
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #48702

## Purpose

`_safe_arg_prefix` included completed middle-field values in `streamed_json` even for non-string-typed keys (integer/boolean/null/number). When `_fix_arg_types` coerced those values at flush time (e.g. `"42"` → `42`, `"true"` → `true`, `"null"` → `null`), the already-sent prefix no longer matched the final JSON, causing `_flush_arg_converter` to silently return `None` and drop the closing brace and any remaining content. Clients received truncated, invalid JSON with no error or log line indicating anything had gone wrong.

**Fix:** during the character scan in `_safe_arg_prefix`, record the position of the first non-string-typed key's value start (`non_string_clip`). After the scan, clip the safe prefix there instead of including it. This ensures the value arrives entirely as a single flush delta after coercion, preserving the `startswith` invariant so the client always accumulates valid, complete JSON.

Affects all parsers using `stream_arg_deltas=True` with an `arg_converter` that cannot parse partial JSON (Qwen3, DeepSeek V4/V32, GLM47, MiniMax, Gemma4, Kimi K2). Parsers that resolve types during streaming itself (e.g. DeepSeek DSML) are structurally unaffected. String-typed fields, already-native-typed values (e.g. unquoted integers), and schemas without a type annotation are unaffected.

This slots in cleanly on top of #46351 (merged). #46351 already protects trailing non-string fields via a dedicated branch in _safe_arg_prefix (the scan's last_key is always the trailing key, so that branch fully covers it) — non_string_clip is never consulted for trailing fields and only fires for middle (comma-terminated) non-string values, which #46351 didn't address. Verified empirically: a trailing non-string field already passes on main; middle non-string fields do not, and pass only with this patch.

- #46351 (merged) — related, complementary; covers trailing values only, not middle fields.

items.title: [Feature] Add PCP O-Proj tensor parallelism
items.bodyExcerpt:
This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-pcp-o-proj-tp` path that shards the resident MLA O-Proj parameter across the combined PCP-by-TP rank grid while preserving the existing TP reduction semantics.

## Summary

The feature further partitions each TP-local O-Proj input shard across the PCP group, reducing the resident O-Proj parameter on each rank to `1 / PCP` of its standard TP layout. Execution requires `decode_context_parallel_size=1` and eager mode.

Supported architectures are DeepSeek V2, V3, and V3.2, plus GLM-4 MoE Lite and the GLM-5 family MLA architecture. Supported O-Proj representations are `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 with a CUTLASS-compatible post-load layout. The NVFP4 adapter is an implementation example for quantized methods; its packed weight and swizzled block scale are handled explicitly. Other post-load layouts fail during post-load processing.

## Runtime behavior

The model runner records the logical, pre-partition batch type and propagates it consistently to every PCP rank. This keeps the collective decision identical even when PCP token partitioning gives different local batch shapes to different ranks.

- For prefill or mixed batches, generic MLA starts an asynchronous O-Proj weight all-gather after Q/KV normalization and before the remaining Q projection, RoPE, indexer, and main attention work. O-Proj waits for the gather only when the full TP shard is needed, then runs the normal TP-local O-Proj computation.
- For decode-only batches, each rank slices the TP attention output to its local PCP feature shard, computes a partial O-Proj result with the resident weight, and all-reduces that result over PCP.
- The existing TP reduction behavior remains unchanged, including paths where TP reduction is handled outside O-Proj.

## Motivation

`GLMGAVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` divides by `source.original_fps` in two places — the duration fallback (`round(max_frame_idx / original_fps) + 1`) and `duration_per_frame = 1 / original_fps` — without validating it. vLLM reports `original_fps == 0` for clips with an unknown or variable frame rate (VFR, malformed containers, failed webcam captures), so those inputs crash with a bare `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`.

items.title: [Kernel] persistent_topk: deterministic select, faster than the exact-topk workaround
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on
   GLM-5.3-Flash across three DGX Sparks and got **9/6 bad turns vs 11/7 stock — within noise**,
   while `index_topk 8192` gives 2/3. Selection accuracy was not their cause
   ([#51782, 09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).

So **the tie-ordering defect is real at the kernel level but does not appear to be reachable on the
traffic that motivated it.** What survives is the performance argument, which is independently
measured: @k3dani fou

items.title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Batch paired KDA gate projections (f_b_proj/g_b_proj) into one bmm
items.bodyExcerpt:
## What

`f_b_proj` and `g_b_proj` in the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer are two same-shape
BF16 GEMMs (`[M, 128] x [128, 1024]` per rank at TP8) applied to adjacent
`head_dim`-wide shards of the merged `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` output. Run them as
one batched GEMM:

- the paired weight is stacked in `process_weights_after_loading`, which runs
  on every load/refit — the stack cannot go stale and no allocation happens
  inside the captured forward;
- inputs are read in place via `as_strided` on the existing projection
  buffer — no copies, no layout change;
- non-BF16 weights keep the two-Linear path.

## Benchmarks (H20, BF16, CUDA graph replay)

Paired f_b+g_b per KDA layer per step: 5.4 -> 4.4 us for M=1..64
(-17% to -22%, decode and spec-verify shapes); no regression at large M
(within 1% at M=8192). Numerics: bit-identical to the two-Linear path
(max_abs_diff = 0, M=1..256).

## Test

- `pytest tests/models/glm5next/` — 15 passed on H20, including the new
  `test_kda_paired_projection.py`: bit-identical vs the two Linears
  (M=1/5/64/256), paired weight rebuilt on re-run of
  `process_weights_after_loading`, disabled for non-BF16 weights.
- Greedy e2e smoke (12 prompts x 256 tokens, temp=0, spec decode on):
  coherent outputs.

Related: #56298 fixes the stale lazy cache for the merged conv weight — this
change builds its paired weight in the post-load hook instead of caching it
in forward. #57318 speeds up a GDN projection with FlashInfer; different op.

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

Pre-commit: all hooks pass. Single-node (TP-only) behavior is untouched — the guards only trigger when the target param is missing.

items.title: [Bugfix] fused_qk_norm_rope: partial rotary neox path shuffled from a divergent branch
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qk_norm_rope` with `rotary_dim < head_dim` (partial rotary, e.g. GLM-4 / GLM-4.5 with `partial_rotary_factor=0.5`) only lets `rotary_lanes = rotary_dim / elems_per_lane` lanes into the RoPE branch. The neox path then calls `__shfl_xor_sync` / `__syncwarp` inside that branch with a full-warp mask, i.e. from a divergent branch where the mask names lanes that never arrive. That is undefined behaviour. With the single-head kernel it happens to produce the right values; with the N-token-heads kernel (`token_heads_per_warp > 1`, auto-selected on SM90 once `num_tokens * (num_heads + num_kv_heads) >= 10240`) it returns garbage or NaN on H200 for such layers.

## Changes

Do the warp exchange once before the lane guard with the whole warp participating; only the rotary lanes use the exchanged values. Same for both kernels. The `__syncwarp()` calls around the shuffle are no longer needed (the shuffle itself synchronises the participating lanes).

## Test plan

Standalone build of this file on H200 against a vLLM 0.28.0 install, compared with that install's `fused_qk_norm_rope`:

- full rotary (`rotary_dim == head_dim`) and all gptj/interleaved cases: bitwise identical to the shipped kernel before and after (bf16/fp16, head_dim 64/128/256, 1–8192 tokens, `token_heads_per_warp` 1/2/4/8).
- partial rotary, neox, e.g. hq32/hkv8/d128 with `rotary_dim=64`: shipped kernel at 300 tokens differs from the fp32 reference by up to 2.9, and is NaN at 2048/8192 tokens; the fixed kernel is finite and matches the fp32 reference at every size (and is still bitwise identical to the shipped kernel wherever `token_heads_per_warp == 1`).

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

items.title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
items.bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) fails to start with any EAGLE-family drafter whose layers are plain sliding-window attention (e.g. the block-diffusion DFlash2 drafter, 5 GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` layers). `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` only accepts exact `MLAAttentionSpec` in the attention group, so it declines; the generic page-size unification then cannot pad the DSA indexer (MLA family) and startup dies:

```
NotImplementedError: indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum
page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers
```

This is the same direction as the draft-group work in #58638 (KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters), applied to the GLM-5.3 builder, which was not covered there.

### Root cause

`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` builds one packed group for `MLAAttentionSpec` + indexer (MLA with `tokens_per_state > 1`) layers and aliases the kpool tails onto the indexer tensors. Its gate requires every non-Mamba / non-`KpoolTailSpec` spec to be exactly `MLAAttentionSpec`. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`KNvfp4Static.process` runs a fused NVFP4 linear (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) under the max of its shards' global weight scales (`weight_scale_2`), and only warns when they differ. Every smaller shard is then dequantized `gs_max / gs_shard` times too large. ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often do differ.

Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16) quantizes the shared experts and dense MLPs. Their gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample, so one projection is inflated by up to 2.5x in every layer for every token. Greedy output stays coherent, which is why this hides. Sampled output at the checkpoint's own defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates into multilingual word salad within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `_reconcile_nvfp4_shard_global_scales`: before the shared max is taken, each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales are multiplied by `gs_shard / gs_max`.

  - Each shard keeps its effective dequant scale within e4m3 rounding.
  - The FP4 payload is unchanged.
- Shared-scale checkpoints are bit-exact no-ops. The previous warning remains for layers whose shard widths (`logical_widths`) cannot be verified against `weight_scale`.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950 device length aware top-k split policy for k=2048
items.bodyExcerpt:
This fixes #55327.

The change generalizes `topKPerRowDecodeGfx950DeviceLengthAware` to work with different values of k, and adds `gfx950TopK2048ActiveBlocks`. The grid still only depends on `numRows`, so graph capture stays stable, and the number of splits is now determined on device per row, ensuring that there are at least 2048 real indices in each split. Rows under 4096 can be processed by a single block, skipping the merge step.

GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 use `index_topk` 2048, which goes through the generic path on gfx950 and has 10 splits. In the merge step, all 20480 candidates are processed by a single block for each row. For rows with fewer active tokens this can lead to significant overhead. With this PR, the number of candidates per row in the merge step will be reduced to between 0 and 12288, a 70 percent reduction in the median case.

I also added two new tests for gfx950 and k 2048, to make sure we're covering the different numbers of splits and graph capture and replay.

I've checked this with a CPU model on all 35 shapes mentioned in the issue, and the result is an exact match with exact top-k for all of them. The kernel compiles fine for gfx950, and I'll provide timings on MI355X in this PR.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can finish startup and still pause to compile an mHC kernel when a new prompt length arrives. This PR moves those missing compilations to startup without changing the kernel math or split-K heuristic.

Addresses #60536. Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/29 for the compile-only entry point used by this implementation.

## Claims

- Register every reachable DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specialization for GLM's configured token range, deduplicated by `(N, K, num_splits)`.
- Compile them through the existing startup warmup registry, without allocating input tensors or launching dummy kernels.
- Keep runtime split selection, kernel math, and backend selection unchanged.

## Details

### Why startup misses these kernels

The mHC pre-norm path contains a matrix multiplication implemented by DeepGEMM. It selects a split-K count (how many pieces to divide the reduction into) based on the number of tokens in the current engine step. Each distinct split count requires a separately compiled kernel. The row count `M` itself is dynamic, so there is no need to compile once per prompt length.

The existing selection is:

```python
num_splits = max(1, min(num_sms // ceil(M / 64), ceil(K / 64) // 4))
```

Here `M` is the step's token count, `K` is the input width, and `N` is the output width. For example, with 78 SMs and `K=16384`, `M=64`, `192`, and `16384` select 64, 26, and 1 splits respectively. Compiling the first and last does not compile the middle one. The number of required specializations depends on the GPU and configured token range; the issue's count of missing variants is not a universal constant.

The startup profile run and CUDA-graph capture exercise only some split counts. GLM does not register the remaining DeepGEMM variants for explicit warmup. items.title: [Perf][DCP] Vectorize SM100 direct Output/LSE consumption
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Speed up the direct symmetric-memory DCP Output/LSE consumer introduced in
#50484. Publication, signaling, allocation, and buffer lifetimes stay unchanged;
this is a focused follow-up from our Shared-DCP work in #50009.

```text
ASIS
publish O/LSE -> signal -> one CTA per head
                          serial peer waits + shared weights -> final O

PR
publish O/LSE -> signal -> four independent warp/head consumers per CTA
                          parallel peer waits + vector loads -> final O
```

## Claims

- On 4x GB200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4 c1 TPOT improved by 2.27% and output throughput
  by 2.07% across two matched fresh-process pairs. c32 serving was neutral.
- Complete direct Output/LSE operator latency improved by 32.4%-40.7% across
  the tested GLM decode shapes, including publication and synchronization.
- No new workspace, communication phase, or runtime option. Dispatch uses the
  warp consumer for SM100-family GPUs, a 512-element value dimension, and at
  most 32 peers. Other devices/layouts retain the existing consumer.

## Validation

items.title: [Attention] Fetch MLA prefill workspace at use instead of init
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The TRTLLM-ragged and FlashInfer MLA prefill backends keep a view of the shared workspace from `__init__`. When a later user, such as the sparse indexer's profile, grows the workspace, that view keeps the old buffer alive as an orphan. On GLM-5.3 on B200 that's 394 MB of GPU memory nobody uses.

Both backends now reserve their size at init without keeping a view, and fetch it in `prepare_metadata`, once per step. FlashInfer rebuilds its wrappers if the workspace has moved. The builder runs outside the DBO micro-batch threads, so both still use the micro-batch 0 slot, as on main.

Sharing the workspace is safe: TRTLLM ragged runs with multi-CTA KV off and uses it only for per-launch softmax stats, and FlashInfer cutlass prefill never touches it (it has its own 32 MB buffer).

## Test Result

Memory: 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV, `--max-model-len 1048576`, TRTLLM-ragged prefill:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV cache | 138.64 GiB | 139.02 GiB |
| GPU KV blocks | 861,476 | 863,866 |
| Orphaned 0.38 GiB block from `trtllm_ragged.py` `__init__` | present | gone |

- Greedy token ids and logprobs are bit-identical to main, with chunked-context prefill, on GLM-5.3 (TRTLLM-ragged) and DeepSeek-V2-Lite (FlashInfer prefill forced). FlashInfer wrappers are built once per backend instance, as on main.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4: main 0.906, this PR 0.908.
- `tests/v1/attention/`: `test_mla_prefill_selector`, `test_mla_prefill_registry`, `test_mla_prefill_quant_output`, `test_mla_noncausal`, `test_sparse_mla_backends`, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla` and `test_mla_backends` all pass on B200.

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Clamp BLOCK_SIZE_K to the FP8 quantization block in the batched Triton MoE
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` (the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE used with DeepEP low-latency and other batched-activation all2all backends when DeepGEMM is unavailable or disabled) takes `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight from the tuned config. With block-quantized FP8 weights the kernel loads one weight and activation scale per `BLOCK_K` tile (`offs_ks = k * BLOCK_K // group_k`), so a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` wider than the 128-wide quantization block applies one block's scale to the next block's values. 53 of the 64 shipped `fp8_w8a8, block_shape=[128,128]` configs pick `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 for some batch sizes. The standard path already clamps (`fused_moe.py:843-844`); this PR applies the same clamp in the batched launcher.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `fused_batched_moe BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K batched fp8`, `batched triton block_shape BLOCK_K`). Rechecked 2026-10-08: open PR #51605 resizes batched Triton MoE tiles on XPU and edits the same launcher, but it does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` for block-quantized FP8 on CUDA; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs from the batched Triton FP8 block-quant MoE whenever the selected config has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` > the quantization block. GLM-5.3 FP8 with DeepEP low-latency and DeepGEMM off: GSM8K 0.02 → 0.93.
- No change when the config already has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` <= 128, for per-token / per-tensor FP8, or for unquantized dtypes (`block_shape is None`).
- A smaller `BLOCK_K` can cost some kernel speed for the affected configs; correctness requires it, and the standard Triton MoE path made the same choice.

## Validation

**Unit test**: `test_batched_mm` (`tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py`) only ever ran FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 32, below the quantization block, so it could not catch this. It now also runs FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256.

items.title: [Perf] Reuse the trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode runner and preallocate its output
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Description

Every sparse-MLA layer calls the FlashInfer `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` wrapper per step with no `out=`. The wrapper re-validates inputs, constructs a fresh `TrtllmGenMlaDecodeRunner` plus `TuningConfig`, runs `AutoTuner.choose_one`, and `torch.empty`s the output (up to 33.5 MB at 4096-row batches), per layer, per step. Under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` attention is an eager break in the piecewise sections, so prefill-mixed steps re-execute that whole Python chain once per sparse layer, about 12 times per engine step.

The runner bakes no query-shape state, so one runner per layer keyed by the KV cache (data_ptr/shape/dtype/top-k capacity) serves every batch. This launches it directly with `tactic=-1` into a per-layer bf16 output buffer sliced per call, with module-scope imports. The DCP path (`return_lse`) keeps the public wrapper because it needs per-call LSE; the HiSparse mixed-step second call gets an `out_offset` so decode and prefill slices stay disjoint before the concat. Runner construction asserts the same two hard constraints the wrapper enforces (head count, block size). Complements #60070 (the counter buffer kwarg) without overlapping it.

Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash (NVFP4), 8x B300 (SM103), TP8, FP8 KV cache, MTP k=7, 1M context, `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, seed 42, medians of 3 warm runs, patch applied alone:

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MLA] Normalize FlashAttention LSE layout in mixed decode/prefill scheduling
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix ROCm MLA chunked-prefill failures by normalizing the log-sum-exp
(LSE) tensor returned by upstream FlashAttention to vLLM's expected
`[num_heads, num_query_tokens]` layout.

Upstream FlashAttention on ROCm returns the LSE tensor as
`[num_query_tokens, num_heads]`. The newer per-request MLA chunk
accumulation path expects the opposite layout. This causes a shape mismatch
when a mixed decode/prefill batch contains a continued prefill.

The normalization is performed at the FlashAttention backend boundary so
the rest of the MLA implementation receives a consistent LSE layout.

## Claims

- Fixes MLA inference crashes on ROCm when chunked prefill produces
  per-request continuation chunks.
- Normalizes upstream FlashAttention LSE output from `[tokens, heads]` to
  vLLM's `[heads, tokens]` contract.
- Preserves the existing CUDA/XPU path, where vLLM FlashAttention already
  returns LSE in the expected layout.
- Does not affect the separate ROCm AITER FlashAttention backend.

## Validation

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Decouple DeepEP low-latency dispatch size from max_num_batched_tokens
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` crashes at startup whenever `--max-num-batched-tokens` is set above a few hundred. This happens with an ordinary prefill-friendly config such as `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. The cause is that the per-rank dispatch capacity of the DeepEP LL buffers is taken directly from `max_num_batched_tokens`. This PR decouples the two: the LL buffers are sized for a fixed number of tokens per rank, and larger forward passes are split into several dispatch rounds that stay in sync across the DP ranks.

Related: #57894 / #57915 (draft). That PR adds a fail-fast error for the same 32 GiB limit, but the config still cannot run. This PR makes the config run.

## Claims

- DP8xEP8 `deepep_low_latency` with `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` now starts and serves correctly with no `NVSHMEM_*` env tuning. Before this PR it crashed in `deep_ep.Buffer.__init__`.
- The memory used by the LL RDMA buffer and the batched-expert workspaces no longer grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- A clear `ValueError` is raised when a user-set `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` is too small. Previously this was a bare `AssertionError` deep inside DeepEP.
- No behavior change for the default LL config: when `max_num_batched_tokens` is not set it already defaults to 256, so no chunking happens and the buffer size is unchanged.
- No behavior change for other all2all backends. Chunking only triggers when a rank's batch exceeds `prepare_finalize.max_num_tokens_per_rank()`. Other prepare/finalize implementations report `max_num_batched_tokens` or `None` there, so they never trigger it.

## Validation

items.title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Register packed MLA KV rows as a single region
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), all layers' pages of a block sit in one contiguous row. 
NIXL still registers one region per layer, so each block moves as one descriptor per layer (effectively rendering BL* useless). 

This PR registers the row once, fixing registration back to its intended use.

Example: GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, BLHNC. Input to `register_kv_caches` on rank 0 is 99 views over one 43.8 GB storage:

```
model.layers.0.self_attn.indexer.k_cache  (14323, 1, 64, 132)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 0
model.layers.0.self_attn.attn             (14323, 1, 64, 576)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 177408
...

row b: [ idx L0 | idx L1 | ... | mla L0 | mla L1 | ... | mla L77 ]   3059712 B
```

**Before** (`elif storage_is_block_major:` branch), each view is its own region:

```
region 0:  base S + 177408, block_len 36864, stride 3059712   # layers.0.attn
region 1:  base S + 0,      block_len 8448,  stride 3059712   # layers.0.indexer
...
-> 99 regions, 99 x 14323 = 1.42M descriptors; a 2-block request = 198 descriptors
```

**After** (the existing whole-row branch, previously push-only), every view emits the same region and dedup folds them into one:

```
region 0:  base S, block_len 3059712, stride 3059712           # whole row, all layers
-> 1 region, 14323 descriptors; a 2-block request = 2 descriptors
```

### HiSparse

A HiSparse decoder can't register rows: its MLA cache is in host DRAM and its indexer on GPU, so it keeps per-layer regions LB*. 
P can still advertise each layer's `(offset, page_size)` within the row (BL*).
When the peer is per-layer, `_split_remote_packed_rows` (added with this PR) maps P's row onto the peer's per-layer regions.
 
BLHNC P + HiSparse D therefore works as before, with the same descriptor count as `main`.

items.title: [HiSparse] Support the FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA backend
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (first sparse MLA choice on Hopper for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash) has no HiSparse path: it converts the logical top-k through `block_table` and reads the layer's paged KV, which holds stale rows for pages HiSparse offloaded. On GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4, H200, prefix caching on) GSM8K degrades across repeated passes on one server: 0.901 → 0.834 → 0.745.

This mirrors the HiSparse branch of the other sparse backends:
- decode rows and resident prefill-only batches: HiSparse physical top-k + hot cache;
- otherwise prefill rows: `stage_prefill_rows` + convert over the staging workspace.

SM90-specific: the backend plans one `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` per batch in `build()`. Decode-only and prefill-only batches keep that single plan (HiSparse's residency output keeps the indexer's valid-prefix layout, which the plan already assumes). Mixed decode + staged-prefill batches read two caches, so with HiSparse the builder plans the prefill rows in a second `_SM90State` (sharing the float workspace); its device `kv_end` clamp takes a row offset so it derives contexts from the right batch rows. Planning stays in `build()`, outside graph capture.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds HiSparse to this backend. Companion: #61243 adds a `supports_hisparse()` capability; whichever lands second sets it to `True` for this backend.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Sync cluster before DSMEM stores in ll_bf16 split-K router GEMM
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The cuteDSL `ll_bf16` split-K router GEMM (#42562, used for M >= 8) writes each CTA's partials into every peer CTA's shared memory (`st.shared::cluster`) before any cluster barrier. CUDA requires a cluster sync before the first DSMEM access, since a peer CTA may not have started yet. When it hasn't, the GPU raises Xid 13 `Graphics SM Cga Exception: CTA Not Present`, which surfaces as `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`.

Fix: a relaxed cluster arrive/wait at kernel start, the same pattern `gemm_rs_ar.py` already uses. No other cuteDSL kernel under `kernels/linear/cute_dsl/` uses DSMEM.

cc @LopezCastroRoberto

## Reproduction

The race depends on timing, and I have no standalone repro on `main`. On H100 (`7fad7db`), none of these attempts triggered it on the unpatched kernel:
- **Stress test:** the split-K GEMM (M ∈ 8–16, K ∈ {4096, 6144, 7168}, N=256, split_k 6/8) in a CUDA graph PDL-chained after a predecessor kernel. Background load mimicked the serving trace: 8–32 streams of small-grid, 1024-thread kernels doing zero-copy reads from pinned host memory, plus random-length spin kernels. ~45M launches, all clean.
- **compute-sanitizer:** memcheck shows no kernel errors with or without the fix. synccheck reports the same pre-existing divergent-barrier warnings in both. racecheck hangs on this kernel in both.

A deterministic test isn't possible from software, because the fault needs the hardware to delay a peer CTA's launch. The fix follows the CUDA DSMEM rule (sync the cluster before the first remote access).

Observed in serving: GLM-5.3 (`RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`) P/D on 2x 8xH200 (coreweave), TP4 decode, PIECEWISE cudagraphs, HiSparse host-pool import forced with `--num-gpu-blocks-override 14000` (HiSparse P/D stack, #55398). Workload: OpenHands-style `swe_smith` multi-turn via evalscope at concurrency 8. The HiSparse DMA streams provide the SM contention.

| unpatched | crashed 4/4 runs within 2 passes;

items.title: [Model] Plumb swiglu_limit through Cohere2Moe
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Cohere2MoeForCausalLM` never constructed a clamped activation. A checkpoint that sets `config.swiglu_limit` still built a bare `SiluAndMul()` and passed no limit into `FusedMoEFactory`, so the clamp never left the model definition.

This is model-definition plumbing only. No kernel change. It mirrors `Glm5NextMLP` / `Glm5NextMoE`:

- dense and shared `Cohere2MoeMLP` take `swiglu_limit` and use `SiluAndMulWithClamp` when the field is set
- the MoE block forwards the same value to `FusedMoEFactory`

This is **clamped SiLU** (`alpha=1.0`, `beta=0.0` defaults), not SwiGLU-OAI.

When `swiglu_limit` is absent, behavior is unchanged: `SiluAndMul()`, and `FusedMoEFactory` receives `None`. No public Cohere checkpoint sets this field today; the PR enables a config field the architecture already documents, the same way GLM-5.Next does.

## Merge ordering

Landing this **before** [ROCm/aiter#6335](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6335) is harmful on gfx942. Today the missing construction is inert. After this PR, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` can send a real limit into `aiter.fused_moe`, land on CK two-stage, and have it **silently dropped**. #6335 is the fail-loud guard for that case. Please do not merge this ahead of that guard without a conscious decision.

This PR does **not** unblock the bf16 → CK path Cohere hits today. That still needs CK kernel work.

## Test plan

- [x] Construction tests in `tests/models/test_cohere2_moe.py` (no GPU):
  - config without `swiglu_limit` → `SiluAndMul`, factory receives `None`
  - config with a finite limit → `SiluAndMulWithClamp` (alpha=1, beta=0) on dense/shared MLP, and the limit reaches `FusedMoEFactory`
- [x] Wired into the CPU Basic Models Other job in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`
